messages:
Ana: hey team — putting together a short compatibility 'charter' for partner SDK/API changes. want a quick sync on the orchestration plan: breaking changes, semver policy, canaries, partner comms windows, and marketplace timing. TL;DR: propose 3 lanes (safe, compatible, breaking) + 6 week partner notice for breaking. thoughts?
Mike: +1 on lanes. can we map lanes to deployment policies? e.g. safe -> auto rollout, compatible -> opt-in canary, breaking -> partner opt-in + gated rollout.
Jess: from eng side we need a clear rollback path and a 'shim' plan for 3rd party SIs and hardware partners. shims should live in a separate repo we can patch independently.
Raj: SDK team: agree on shim repo. also want to standardize headers and error codes before we ship any change. can we commit to a single http header for compatibility level like `x-rw-compat`?
Olivia: partners care about marketplace listings and joint announcements. they need a minimum of 8 weeks for co-announcements and a 4 week marketplace embargo window if change affects billing or API contract. can we make those timelines explicit in the charter?
Ana: noted. proposed timeline matrix: breaking changes = 6 week technical notice + 8 week comms window if joint announcement + 2 week marketplace freeze prior to announce. compatible changes = 2 week notice + canary week. safe = immediate (no notice).
Mike: operationally we should attach a rollout policy: traffic % progression, observability gates, and automatic fallback to previous model / runtime when latency or error rate spikes. suggest automation steps: 0% -> 5% -> 25% -> 100% with 24h at each stage and automatic rollback on >=1.5x error rate or >20% latency P95 increase.
Jess: add a dark-run stage for SI integrations: route mirrored traffic to partner envs for 1 week before canary. helps catch infra-specific regressions for hardware partners.
Raj: SDK changes — we'll publish a compat matrix and provide migration helpers. sample header we plan to use in SDKs: `Accept-Compatibility: 2026-compat-v2` (will parse on server to choose behavior).
Olivia: partners also want a migration sandbox and an integration health scoreboard (uptime, API errors, sample call latency). can devex own the scoreboard dashboard?
Ana: yes, devex will spin up a shared sandbox and a scoreboard. Raj — can you commit to publishing the compat matrix and a small migration script (node/python) within 2 weeks?
Raj: yes. we'll generate a `compat-matrix.json` and a simple `migrate.sh` that updates usage of deprecated endpoints. example curl we'll include in the doc:
```
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \ 
     -H "Accept-Compatibility: 2026-compat-v2" \ 
     https://api.redwood.inference/v1/partners/echo
```
Olivia: communication plan: partner notification email -> partner-only webinar -> public docs -> marketplace announcement. timeline example for a breaking change: notice(week0) -> webinar(week3) -> sandbox(week4-6) -> marketplace freeze(week7-8) -> public announce(week8).
Mike: security/compliance note: any private deployment partners must sign off on API change through an escalation alias (partners-sig@redwood). include a checklist item for KMS/HSM compatibility testing.
Jess: QA checklist items: unit tests, contract tests against `compat-matrix.json`, canary smoke tests, integration tests with shim + hardware partners, and a post-rollout eval run to track quality regressions.
Ana: decision items for this thread: (1) accept lanes + timelines above, (2) Raj to publish matrix + migrate scripts in 2 weeks, (3) Devex to create sandbox + scoreboard, (4) create partner escalation alias and comms template. if no objections i'll lock the charter and file a partner-runbook PR by EOD Friday.
Raj: no objections from SDK team. 2-week commit noted.
Olivia: ack from partnerships. will draft comms templates and partner webinar invite.
Mike: ops acked, will draft rollout automation playbook and canary thresholds in runbook.
Jess: eng ack. i'll add QA checklist to the PR.
deploy-bot: deployment scheduled: partner-charter-doc -> staging at 2026-05-12T09:00:00Z (preview link: https://ci.redwood.dev/preview/partner-charter).
Ana: thanks everyone — i'll open the PR now and tag owners. small follow-ups in thread: who owns monitoring alerts for partner scorecards?
Olivia: partnerships will own outreach + alert ownership for partner scorecards (oncall rotation to be defined).
Mike: ops will own the infra alerts (latency/error gates). we'll coordinate on slack alias.
Ana: perfect. locking this plan unless anyone raises a blocker before EOD Friday. :lock:
